column8: Wed 18 Nov: store, input to row 16's contrast for 3a: aircraft reserves are collected monthly by use for named future costs, while Laura's are bought at once in January 2027 and January 2028 for ten named payments (IPS l.13); 10-K read at source.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a evidence for row 16's contrast: the lessor releases only on an invoice it approves and keeps what is never claimed, while each Treasury pays on its date with no one's approval and what is left is Laura's ($75,934 by 1 Jan 2042 at forwards, NUMBERS 8h, checks); carries rows 4 and 12.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; the scale and the about 18% paid out (Keel arithmetic) mix security deposits with reserves, so never quote the share as reserves released; serves no part.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 2 (unclaimed reserves become the lessor's income); adds only the $69.2m line, which also holds end-of-lease payments, so never quote it as unclaimed reserves alone.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a aha candidate behind row 16 (3a's spine slot is AHA row 5, so an alternative, never an addition): a lessor asks reserves of the lessees whose credit it trusts least; cite IPS l.9 for her career as shares she cannot sell and l.11 for the ladder (no payment depends on anybody else's money), never l.9 as the ladder's reason; AerCap read in extracts only.

Wed 18 Nov: store only; AerCap's revenue test matches Keel's escrow-release reading ($59,835 in all, NUMBERS 8h, checks), but any yearly release is Keel's reading and the IPS is silent, so never as the plan; accounting words, hard to say plainly.

Wed 18 Nov: store, the primary source for row 16's whose security: IATA calls reserves security held by the lessor, sized from an estimated cost; Laura's rungs need no estimate, each payment is a fixed $50,000; carries row 11.

Wed 18 Nov: store or Figure 1's note: one account per event against Laura's pooled extra Treasuries; $2,662 to $7,820 is Figure 1's world (cash waiting earns nothing, with the bill fund's fee, NUMBERS 8h, checks); in prose the extra Treasuries, never backstop (WORDS).

Wed 18 Nov: store; release-on-proof reserves are fought over at the proof step (work scope), which Laura's maturities do not have; her own weak points are Table 3 row 4's (a fund ending early, waiting cash), so never say her reserve has no weak point.

Wed 18 Nov: store, evidence for row 16: a filed engine lease puts three gates on each release (no default, a deadline, an invoice) and keeps the balance; Laura's releases have none; quote one gate at most.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 7 (reserves are the lessor's property once paid), from a consultant's primer; its no-transfer point repeats row 8; held for her (Q72) stays the plan's words.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 2 (the holder profits from the release rules); one law firm's view, with its own perhaps.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a store or one clause on how the reserve is held: three custody choices (the other side, a third party, yourself), and Laura holds her own at one broker (Q78), where a failure means delay, not loss (Q72); page extract only; carries row 15.

Wed 18 Nov: store, 3e at most: a reserve fed from future income stops with it (Avianca); fix filled before any promise, wrong since the ten are owed from the start: say most of each payment owned from January 2027 and all ten from January 2028, five years before the first, with the 2028 deposit the one part still to come (IPS l.17's missed deposit).
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 13's insolvency point (reserve money treated as the holder's estate); paywalled after the opening, so it adds only the 2004 date.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a, one plain sentence on how the reserve pays out: whose security it is, who can refuse a release and what triggers it (an approved invoice against a maturity date and nobody's approval; IPS l.13, NUMBERS 8h); a contrast, never a claim that aircraft reserves fail.

Wed 18 Nov: CONCEIT store only: 3a's one turn is spoken for (the line that waited in pencil, V2.2), so this could only replace it, never add; never call the airline's reserve pencil, which stretches the definition: say the fact plainly (the lessor owns it and pays on an invoice it approves) beside ink for Laura's payments.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q55-016 (MacArthur's expected schedule and progress gate) and Q55-014; Mott adds projected dates and interim reports before each payment, which row 24 carries.

Wed 18 Nov: store, fills Q55's missing Mellon letter (schedule, reports and a right to stop in one letter); drop the largest US arts funder unless read at source; a sample, its schedules not attached.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e store, answers who signs: in grant practice the receiver's officer signs and the payer can stop; for Laura only the receipt is useful (row 45); an eight-month grant, so never as multi-year evidence.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a or 3d's half-clause: Ford's new multi-year floor (9 Nov 2026) runs three to five years, so Laura's ten owned years are twice its top; updates Q55-045's term list (Ford BUILD 5); owned at today's rates as most of each payment from January 2027 and all ten from January 2028.

Wed 18 Nov: store; Ford honours grants already made, so the contrast is renewal, never a broken promise; drop a change of mind is not one, which reads IPS l.17 as a lock on Laura: the two reasons and the ways a promise fails are two lists (Q109); the Chronicle read in extract only.

Wed 18 Nov: store or 3d beside row 21: most of Ford's flexible grants run one or two years (Inside Philanthropy's summary of Ford's figures); drop likely about the residency's other money, which no source gives; say only how one large funder writes its terms.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e or 3a, one clause with a judge's turn: in every agreement read (Mott, Mellon, Ford/IIE; Q55's Hewlett, Kresge, MacArthur) the report unlocks the next payment; Laura's next payment is already bought, so her yearly report records and unlocks nothing.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q73-030 (pledge schedules run five years, Penn); Michigan and Cal Poly Pomona add two more names and the unconditional acknowledgement only.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d half-clause store: a public university takes pledges of five years and ten only case by case; with row 27 the clearest proof that ten years is the edge of what fundraisers accept as a promise, while Laura's ten are owned, not promised from income.

Wed 18 Nov: store beside row 26: one public counting rule books only the first five years of a longer pledge; an internal reporting rule, not accounting law (Q55-034), so never as how co-sponsors must count Laura's ten.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d guard, the fundraisers' own rule: only the entity with legal control over the assets can pledge, matching IPS l.15's money you already own; CASE read only as quoted by SFSU, so cite SFSU.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e store for row 45: a three-line receipt (promised, paid to date, still due) is the shape of the residency's yearly confirmation; its commitment-words point is Q18-004's twin and stays there.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: pledges need a collection office (reminders at 30, 60 and 90 days, write-off approvals), Laura's payments only a transfer instruction; a receiver's procedure, beside Q53-018.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q53-018, which already quotes Cal Poly Pomona's two years beyond the last date; adds only the CEO's signature.

Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q55-041 (merged into Q18-031): a DAF's schedule rides on markets and its trustees may refuse; analogy only, since any DAF would move the money out of Laura's ownership and change the frozen plan; quotes through a page summary.

Wed 18 Nov: store; the strictest set-aside is outside the owner's control by law, while Laura's sits in her control and is protected by what it holds (Treasuries); the IPS's two reasons say when the plan changes, never what protects it (Q109).

Wed 18 Nov: store only: notice to a regulator 30 working days before any withdrawal; Laura has no one to notify and public maturity dates are a weak parallel; Table 3 row 4 already watches the funds' own notices.

Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q16-022 (a regulator's periodic sufficiency report on a dedicated reserve); the NRC's lines (amount required, funds held, schedule, assumptions) add a federal source to the lines Q16-039 already sets.

Wed 18 Nov: store only; fix no signature can redirect it before its date, which is false: Laura can sell any holding before it matures; say instead that no one's signature is needed for each Treasury to pay.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; a lender-held building reserve released on invoice belongs to the facility's financing, out of scope (case A13), never to Laura's reserve.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; a staged release after inspection protects the public against an operator; a weak parallel to ten dated releases.

Wed 18 Nov: store only, analogy only: Taiwan's public-interest trust needs a supervisor who reviews a yearly report; Taiwan law is context only (case A13), and no trust is ever offered for Laura (the IPS is frozen).
Wed 18 Nov: store only: drop the CONCEIT use, since the seal is out of the conceit (a seal is a signature, Q121); a multi-owner building fund, Taiwan law context only (A13).

Wed 18 Nov: 3a or 3.0 Client Knowledge store beside Q22-026: adds who held Artpace's founder money (her foundation, through an annuity for up to 20 years) and its 2022 end ($1,196,000 advanced); Laura's ten have one holder, herself; 3.0's evidence slot is Q118-009, so never both.
Wed 18 Nov: store, analogy only beside row 41: founder to lead trust to foundation to residency, $600,000 a year in 2019 and 2020; a lead trust is never offered for Laura (frozen IPS; Q55-042, Q70).

Wed 18 Nov: store only, never in the report: an aggregator's view of one named foundation's filing with unexplained payables; drop founder pays as she goes, an inference the data does not support (the row's own critique).

Wed 18 Nov: 3a notes on how the reserve is held and paid out: who holds (case l.95, checked), what releases (8 to 14 and 47 to 318 days, NUMBERS 8h, checks), who can refuse (nobody); $445,655 and 111.7% are printed once, in Figure 1's note (density cut), never in 3a's prose; in prose the extra Treasuries, never backstop.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e, one clause: Table 3 watches the Treasury paying Laura and nothing watches Laura paying the residency (checked in exhibits/tables.md); keep the January instruction and the residency's receipt (row 29) only; the after-her line and Taiwan's public list are case A13 context (Q55-044's note), never advice.
